Hi @SteveMacenski


I tested the nav2_smac_planner package using the Hybrid A* method, and the issue described in #5192 no longer appears.


But I noticed some very similar behavior near the end of the path (though it doesn't happen very frequently, it might happen once every 20 runs or so,). It looks like the robot is reversing, and the path segments are very short, usually concentrated in the last one or two nodes. I'm not sure if this is expected behavior, or if it might be caused by a high reverse penalty I set in the parameters (reverse_penalty: 300.0).

As I mentioned in #5192 (comment) this is expected and correct behavior. We want to be able to do this (that is the point of reeds shepp paths)! That is the shortest path to the goal.


The goal of this PR to make it less likely that we have those trivial reversal changes by not allowing refinements to create more of them -- and if a refinement can create less, we prioritize that. But sometimes that may legitimately be necessary as in the cases you show in the requested orientation.
